title: Debugging Performance Issues
description: Systematic approach to diagnosing runtime performance problems using Chrome DevTools, Lighthouse, and targeted reproduction techniques.

data.text: Performance debugging is not random poking in DevTools. It is a systematic process: reproduce the issue, isolate the slow code path, form a hypothesis, test one change, and verify with before/after measurements. The best debuggers work from evidence, not guesses.

Before debugging anything, you must reproduce it. Create a minimal scenario that reliably shows the jank, long task, or layout shift. Record a screen capture or save a HAR file so the issue can be shared and compared.

data.title: Reproduction Checklist
data.content: Steps to capture a reliable reproduction.
data.code:
Reproduction checklist:

1. Identify the exact user flow: route, component, interaction
2. Note device, browser version, and network conditions
3. Open DevTools with all relevant panels: Performance, Network, Console
4. Disable cache and enable CPU / network throttling
5. Record the interaction from start to finish
6. Save the trace (Export HAR / trace JSON)
7. Document: what you expected vs what happened
8. Share the trace with teammates if needed

Throttling settings in DevTools:
- CPU: 4x slowdown (simulates mid-range mobile)
- Network: Fast 3G / Slow 3G
- Disable cache: forces real network behavior

data.text: DevTools provides multiple panels that surface different kinds of performance data. Use the Performance panel for frame-level analysis, Network for asset timing, Lighthouse for automated audits, and the Memory panel for leak investigation.

data.title: DevTools Panel Cheat Sheet
data.content: What each panel is best for diagnosing.
data.code:
Performance panel:
- Frame rate, long tasks, forced layout
- Flame charts, call trees, event log
- Screenshots and frame screenshots

Network panel:
- Waterfall of requests
- Identify slow assets, render-blocking resources
- Check cache headers, compression, priority

Lighthouse panel:
- Automated audits for LCP, INP, CLS
- Actionable recommendations with code snippets
- CI-ready, reproducible scores

Memory panel:
- Heap snapshots for leaks
- Allocation instrumentation on timeline
- Detached DOM nodes

Console / Command Menu:
- $0 for inspected element
- copy() to grab values
- getEventListeners() to audit listeners

data.text: Most runtime performance bugs fall into a small set of categories: long tasks, layout thrashing, excessive paint, memory leaks, and third-party script interference. Each has a recognizable signature in DevTools.

data.title: Issue Signatures in DevTools
data.content: Recognize and fix common runtime performance problems.
data.code:
Symptom: Page feels sluggish on scroll
Likely cause: Long tasks, layout thrashing, heavy paint
DevTools:
- Performance: long yellow scripting blocks
- Performance: red forced layout bars
- Rendering: paint flashing on many elements
Fix: reduce JS work, batch reads/writes, simplify paint

Symptom: Animations stutter
Likely cause: Layout-triggering properties, GC pauses
DevTools:
- Performance: layout/paint every frame
- Memory: heap spikes during animation
Fix: animate transform/opacity only, reduce allocations

Symptom: Tab crashes after extended use
Likely cause: Memory leak
DevTools:
- Memory: heap grows and never shrinks
- Memory: detached DOM nodes accumulate
Fix: find leak pattern, add cleanup, verify with heap snapshots

Symptom: Slow first interaction after page load
Likely cause: Large JS bundles, event delegation missing
DevTools:
- Network: huge main bundle
- Performance: long task on first click
Fix: code split, lazy load, remove main-thread work

data.text: Lighthouse automates many common runtime performance checks and gives prioritized recommendations. Run it in DevTools for quick feedback and in CI to catch regressions before they ship.

data.title: Lighthouse Runtime Audits
data.content: Use Lighthouse to find quick wins.
data.code:
Key Lighthouse runtime audits:

- Reduce unused JavaScript
  > Identify large bundles with low coverage
  > Action: code split, dynamic imports

- Avoid enormous network payloads
  > Total bytes transferred
  > Action: compress, tree-shake, lazy load

- Minimize main-thread work
  > Total blocking time estimate
  > Action: break up long tasks, defer work

- Reduce JavaScript execution time
  > Script evaluation time
  > Action: defer non-critical scripts

- Avoid large layout shifts
  > CLS contributors
  > Action: reserve image/ad space, avoid font flashes

Running Lighthouse in CI:
- npx lighthouse <url> --view
- Use lhci (Lighthouse CI) for thresholds and history

data.text: React DevTools Profiler shows component render times, why components re-rendered, and which commits were wasted. Combine it with Chrome's Performance panel to see whether slow renders come from React itself or from layout and paint.

data.title: React Profiler Diagnosis
data.content: Use React DevTools Profiler to isolate slow components.
data.code:
React DevTools Profiler workflow:

1. Open React DevTools > Profiler tab
2. Click Record
3. Interact with the app
4. Stop recording
5. Inspect:
   - Flamegraph: component render times
   - Ranked chart: most expensive commits
   - Interactions: per-interaction breakdown

What to look for:
- Components with high 'Self time'
- 'Why did this render?' → props, state, context changes
- Commits that took >16 ms
- Unnecessary renders of large lists

Common React performance fixes:
- Memoize expensive list items with React.memo
- Move state down to leaf components
- Split context to avoid broad re-renders
- Virtualize long lists with react-window

data.title: Optimize After You Profile
data.text: Premature optimization wastes time and introduces bugs. Profile first, identify the bottleneck, then apply a targeted fix. A single unnecessary re-render is not worth rewriting your state management unless it is measurable.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Reproduce performance issues reliably before debugging
Use Performance panel for frame-level analysis of long tasks and layout
Use Network panel for asset timing and render-blocking resources
Use Lighthouse for automated audits and quick wins
Use React Profiler to isolate unnecessary re-renders
Always compare before and after measurements
Capture and share traces (HAR / trace JSON) for reproducibility
data.takeaway: Systematic debugging beats random guessing. Reproduce, isolate, hypothesize, test one change, and verify with evidence.
